The function $f(x)$ is defined and differentiable on the interval $[-4,4].$ The graph of $y={f}^{′}(x),$ the derivative of $f(x),$ is given above, where the areas of the regions between the graph and the $x$-axis are $8,5$ and $6,$ respectively (from left to right). Find $f(4)$ if $f(-4)=-1.$
question.worked_solution:
From the fundamental theorem of calculus, we find that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-4}^{4}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x & =f(4)-f(-4) \\ {\int }_{-4}^{4}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x & =f(4)-(-1) \\ f(4) & =-1+{\int }_{-4}^{4}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, remember that the integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where we take the area as negative if the curve lies below the $x$-axis. So, using the labels on the graph, the integral is

$$
{\int }_{-4}^{4}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x=8+(-5)+6=9.
$$

Finally, using the value of the integral, we can find $f(4):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(4) & =-1+{\int }_{-4}^{4}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-1+9 \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$
